# tutor


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module runs the learning loop.
[`pick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/model.html#pick) chooses
the concept and the depth, and a model writes the question. The learner
answers and can ask for hints. The model grades the answer, and the
learner model updates the concept. After a miss, the tutor teaches the
smallest step. Each surface (the web app, the ramabana terminal agent, a
notebook) uses
[`Tutor`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor) and
[`Session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#session).

Import the tools that this module uses, and the other abhyasa modules
that the tutor calls.

## Tries and hints

A wrong answer does not end the question. The tutor names the first
error, gives no fix, and the learner tries again. After the tries of the
setting `checks.tries` (3 by default), or when the learner stops, the
tutor teaches the smallest step. Then the state of the concept records
the miss. A pass after a wrong try counts as `fragile`. The best try
counts: each try keeps its grade. When a try had the grade of
`checks.near` (7 by default) or more, the close is a `fragile` pass, not
a miss, because the learner had the idea.

Each open question keeps a thread, `q.turns`: the question, then each
message of the learner and each reply of the tutor, in order. A message
of the learner is only what they say this time, often a follow-up to the
last nudge. They do not send the full answer again. The grade, the hints
and the lesson read the whole thread.

`HINTS` is the hint ladder, from the least to the most revealing. The
model gets one rung for each hint request.

`DEPTH_ASK` tells the model what a question at each depth must make the
learner do. It is the prompt `depths`, one line for each depth, so you
can change it on the Settings page.
[`depth_ask`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#depth_ask)
reads it when a question is written.

`TUTOR_SP` is the system prompt for questions, hints and lessons.

The page renders markdown. So the prompt asks for maths between `$...$`
and for code in a fenced block with its language. Then a question with
code keeps its lines.

``` python
assert 'between $...$ for maths' in TUTOR_SP
assert 'fenced code block' in TUTOR_SP and '```python' in TUTOR_SP
```

## Prompts

Each prompt function makes the text for one model call. The prompt text
is an instruction to the model.

`QUESTION_RULES` is the fixed instruction for each new question. A
question asks one thing, in under 60 words and in plain words. Pairs of
a bad and a good question show each rule.
[`asks_twice`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#asks_twice)
is a quick check on a written question: it finds a second ask after a
comma, or a second question mark.

A transfer question asks the learner to use an idea in a new place. The
best new place is one that they already know.
[`bridges`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#bridges)
names up to three concepts that the learner knows to depth 3 or more:
from other subjects first, then linked ones, then the deepest. Thus a
transfer question on attention can use a Sanskrit or jyotiṣa idea.

## Prompts that you can change

The instruction text of each prompt is in the registry of `prompts`, so
you can change it in Settings. The constants stay as the defaults. A
prompt function reads the text when it runs, so a change works on the
next question.
[`hints`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#hints) gives
the hint ladder in use. A saved ladder must have 6 lines, and a lesson
instruction must keep the ‘Check:’ line.

## Open questions on the shelf

The tutor keeps each open question in memory, and also on the shelf as a
document of kind `open-q`. The document has the full question: the text,
the concept, the kind, the options, the answer key, the tries, the
hints, the confidence, the session and the walk step. Only the server
reads it. A restart of the app thus loses no open question.

`put_open_q` writes the document under the lock of the question. A
closed question stays on the shelf with its status and its end
(`closed`, `dropped` or `abandoned`), so that an old copy, such as the
open question in a session document, cannot open it again. `open_q`
reads it.

## Ask a question

`ask_on` uses the first source that it finds: the check from the last
lesson, a ready question, or a new question from the model. It shuffles
the options of a choice question, and starts the thread with the
question.
[`public`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#public)
removes the fields that the learner must not see.

A question with code gets the code in a fenced block first, so its lines
stay. A question without code stays as it is.

``` python
q = with_code('What does it return?', 'def f(x):\n    return x + 1')
assert q.startswith('```python\ndef f(x):\n    return x + 1\n```') and q.endswith('What does it return?')
assert with_code('Why?', '') == 'Why?'
assert '"code": str' in question_prompt(dict(name='n', slug='n'), 2)
```

A question that asks twice is written again one time, with the first try
in the prompt. The test gives a paired question first, then a single
one.

``` python
for q in ('What must the arrow carry, and why does the right box need it?', 'Which team matches a recurrent model, and why?', 'What moves, and what stays fixed?', 'Why? What?'): assert asks_twice(q), q
for q in ('What is X, and how is it used?', 'What is X or how is it used?'): assert asks_twice(q), q
for q in ('Why does it print 7, not 8?', 'A user, who types fast, sends two lines. Which line arrives first?', 'If the list is sorted, what does f return?',
          'When x is 3, why does f print 7?', 'In a loop with n items, how many calls happen?', 'For the input 5, where does the value go?'): assert not asks_twice(q), q   # a clause first is one ask
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
paired = iter([dict(question='What moves, and what stays fixed?', answer='a', rubric=['a']), dict(question='What stays fixed?', answer='a', rubric=['a'])])
lr = temp_learning(); c = lr.put('Fixed point', 'A point that stays.', 'ml')
fk = Fake(dflt=lambda p, sp: next(paired))
t = Tutor(lr, fk, sources=[]); q = t.ask_on(c, 3, method='words')
test_eq(q.question, 'What stays fixed?'); test_eq(len(fk.calls), 2)
assert 'asked twice' in fk.calls[1][0] and 'What moves, and what stays fixed?' in fk.calls[1][0]
```

note says why, so the learner sees the change.

## Hints

Each call to `hint` gives the next rung of the ladder. After the last
rung, it gives the last hint again.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```

*The next hint on the ladder, from the least to the most revealing.*

A board of the screen guide on an open check counts as one hint, as a
hint from the ladder does: `board_hint` keeps the words of the board as
the next hint, with `via='board'`, and gives the count of hints. When
the ladder is used up, it keeps nothing and gives None.

## Grade an answer

`_grade` grades a choice question in code and other questions with the
model.

`answer` adds the message of the learner to the thread, and the nudge
after a wrong try. A pass or the last try closes the question.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Grade an answer. A wrong try keeps the question open with a nudge. A
pass or the last try closes it and updates the concept.*

## Stop and teach

`give_up` closes the question as a miss, unless an earlier try was
graded `checks.near` or more.
[`_close`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/talk.html#_close)
updates the concept, teaches after a miss and records the attempt.
Before the lesson, a function in `LESSON_HOOKS` can pick another way for
the lesson. The result names that way in
[`lesson_way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#lesson_way).
Then each function in `CLOSE_HOOKS` can add to the result. The demo
module uses this hook to attach a demo after a miss. The confidence of
the first try counts, because the first try shows what the learner
believed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### give_up

``` python
def give_up(
    qid:str, confidence:int=0, dont_know:bool=False
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Close the question as a miss and teach the smallest step. A shown
answer is a miss, unless a try had a grade of `checks.near` or more.*

`_lesson` writes the lesson after a miss. When the model fails, the
lesson is a note with the model answer.

## A session

[`Session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#session)
keeps one sitting together. Its id goes on each attempt, and it stops
after `limit` questions (by default, the session length in the profile
of the learner). It asks about one concept for at most `run` questions
in a row. This lets the range between floor and ceiling close, and it
keeps the learner interested.

A session is saved on the shelf after each move: when a question opens,
after each answer and hint, and at the end. It keeps the log of each
closed question (with the floor before and after, and the thread) and
the open question with its thread. Thus
[`Session.load`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#session.load)
continues it after a restart, with the same question, graded the same
way.

A session in a walk asks about the current step of the walk. When the
step is learned, the next question is on the next step.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/tutor.py#L566"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Session

``` python
def Session(
    tutor:__main__.Tutor, focus:str=None, subject:str=None, limit:int=None, run:int=3, journey:str=None,
    sid:str=None, drill:bool=False
):
```

*One sitting: questions and answers, saved on the shelf after each move,
so that a restart can continue it.*

A check right after a lesson shows that you understood it. It does not
show that you will remember it, because the lesson is still in your
mind. Thus each concept that you miss in a session comes back one more
time before the end. At least two other questions come between the miss
and the retest.
[`retests`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#retests)
finds these concepts. A pass right after the miss does not count.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### retests

``` python
def retests(
    log, gap:int=None
)->dict:
```

*The concepts missed in a session log, with no pass at least `gap`
questions after the miss: concept -\> its last miss, oldest first.*

`_retest` asks one of them when only enough questions are left to retest
each miss once.

A drill session (“Practice my weak spots”) asks your weakest concepts
first, each one time, with your best method. When none is left, the
session goes on as usual.

`answer`, `give_up` and `hint` act on the open question and save the
session. A closed question goes in the log with what moved.

closes the session. `load` reads a session back, with its open question.

### moved

``` python
def moved(
    log
)->list:
```

*For each concept in a session log, in order: its name, the floor before
and after, and the misconceptions found.*

## Tests

A fake model plays the tutor. Its grader passes an answer only when the
answer has the words “rank position”. Two concepts are on the shelf, and
`Reciprocal rank fusion` needs `Ranking`.

``` python
from abhyasa.store import temp_learning
from abhyasa.llm import Fake
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
lr.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml', order=0)
lr.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Merge ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank).', 'ml', prereqs=['ranking'], order=1)
def grader(p, sp):
    ok = 'rank position' in p.split("Learner's answer:")[1]
    return dict(correct=ok, grade=8 if ok else 3, first_error='You add raw scores.',
                               misconception='scores are comparable across systems', feedback='Look at what each list really shares.')
fake = Fake({'You grade one answer': grader, 'Give hint level': 'Look at what the two lists have in common.',
             'Teach the smallest step': 'Only positions are shared. Check: what happens with k = 0?',
             'Write ONE question': dict(question='Why does RRF use ranks, not scores?', answer='Scores are not comparable.', rubric=['ranks are comparable'])})
t = Tutor(lr, fake, context=False)
```

The first question is on the prereq, at depth 3. The learner does not
see the answer or the rubric.

``` python
q = t.next()
test_eq((q.concept, q.depth, q.kind), ('ranking', 3, 'explain'))   # rrf waits for its prereq
assert 'answer' not in q and 'rubric' not in q
```

A wrong answer keeps the question open and names the first error. Then a
hint comes from the ladder.

``` python
r = t.answer(q.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=90)
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.tries_left), (False, False, 2))
test_eq(r.first_error, 'You add raw scores.')
test_eq(t.hint(q.id), 'Look at what the two lists have in common.')
```

A pass after a wrong try and a hint is `fragile`. The floor stays, and
the concept is `shaky` at depth 3.

``` python
r = t.answer(q.id, 'use the rank position', thinking='positions are shared', confidence=90)
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.outcome), (True, True, 'fragile'))   # passed, but after a wrong try and a hint
c = lr.concept('ranking')
test_eq((c.floor, c.shaky, c.seen), (0, 3, 1))
test_eq(len(lr.attempts('ranking')), 2)
```

The thread holds each turn in order: the question, the wrong try, its
nudge, the hint and the pass.

``` python
test_eq([(x['who'], x.get('kind')) for x in q.turns],
        [('tutor', 'question'), ('you', None), ('tutor', 'nudge'), ('tutor', 'hint'), ('you', None), ('tutor', 'close')])
test_eq(lr.attempts('ranking')[0].thread[1]['text'], 'sum the scores')   # the final attempt keeps the thread
```

A board on an open check is one hint. The grade counts it, as it counts
each hint:

``` python
bl = temp_learning(); bl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
bt = Tutor(bl, fake, context=False)
bq = bt.ask_on(bl.concept('ranking'), 2)
test_eq(bt.board_hint(bq.id, 'The board circled the two ranks.'), 1)
test_eq((bt.open[bq.id].hints, bt.open[bq.id].turns[-1]['via']), (['The board circled the two ranks.'], 'board'))
for _ in range(len(HINTS) - 1): bt.board_hint(bq.id, 'Again.')
test_eq(bt.board_hint(bq.id, 'One too many.'), None)
```

Three wrong tries close the question, keep the misconception and teach.

``` python
q = t.next(focus='ranking')
test_eq(q.depth, 3)    # shaky at explain: ask at explain again
for _ in range(3): r = t.answer(q.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=85)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'misconception'))
assert 'Check:' in r.lesson
c = lr.concept('ranking')
test_eq((c.ceiling, c.misconceptions), (3, ['scores are comparable across systems']))
```

When the lesson model fails, the question still closes, the miss counts
once, and the lesson says what happened.

``` python
fl = temp_learning(); fl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
def broken(p, sp=''):
    if 'Teach the smallest step' in p: raise RuntimeError('the model is down')
    return fake(p, sp)
ft = Tutor(fl, broken, context=False)
q = ft.next()
for a in ('sum the scores', 'add the scores', 'average the scores'): r = ft.answer(q.id, a, confidence=85)
test_eq((r.done, q.id in ft.open), (True, False))
assert 'could not write the lesson' in r.lesson and 'Scores are not comparable' in r.lesson
c = fl.concept('ranking')
test_eq((c.seen, c.misses), (1, 1))
test_eq(len([a for a in fl.attempts('ranking') if a.get('final')]), 1)
```

The check question from the lesson comes next.

``` python
q = t.next(focus='ranking')
test_eq(q.question, 'what happens with k = 0?')   # the lesson's check comes next
t.open.clear()
```

A ready question from a source comes before a question from the model.

``` python
lr.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', questions=[dict(q='Join na + asti.', a='nāsti', depth=3)])
q = t.next(subject='sanskrit')
test_eq(q.question, 'Join na + asti.')
```

Code grades a choice question. A wrong option gives the misconception
that it matches.

``` python
fake.rules['Write ONE question'] = dict(question='Which is a sandhi?', options=[dict(text='na + asti → nāsti', misconception=''),
    dict(text='na + asti → naasti', misconception='vowels just sit side by side')], correct=0, answer='', rubric=[])
t.open.clear()
lr.update('sandhi', floor=0, ceiling=2)
q = t.next(subject='sanskrit')
test_eq(q.kind, 'choice')
r = t.answer(q.id, q.options.index('na + asti → naasti'), confidence=90)
test_eq(r.first_error, 'This option assumes: vowels just sit side by side')
```

A session stops after `limit` questions and files a summary.

``` python
fake2 = Fake({k: fake.rules[k] for k in ('You grade one answer', 'Teach the smallest step')},
             dflt=dict(question='What does a rank tell you?', answer='Its position.', rubric=['position']))
s = Session(Tutor(temp_learning(), fake2, context=False), limit=2)
s.tutor.learning.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
assert s.next() is not None
s.give_up()
assert s.next() is not None
test_eq(s.answer('the rank position', confidence=80).correct, True)
test_eq(s.next(), None)
test_eq(s.summary(), '1 of 2 passed. Concepts: ranking.')
test_eq(s.tutor.learning.session(s.id).asked, 2)          # filed as it goes, not only at the end
```

A session on one concept stays in its subject. It asks about the
neighbors of the concept first.

``` python
sl = temp_learning()
sl.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml', order=0)
sl.put('Softmax', 'Turns scores into weights that sum to 1.', 'ml', related=['attention'], order=5)
sl.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', order=0)
ss = Session(Tutor(sl, fake2, context=False), focus='attention')
test_eq((ss.subject, ss.near), ('ml', {'softmax'}))
sl.update('attention', floor=4, seen=1, due=1e12)   # learned, and not due: the session moves on, and stays in ml
test_eq(ss.next().concept, 'softmax')
```

A session is saved with its open question. `load` continues it in a new
tutor, as after a restart, and grades the same question.

``` python
pl = temp_learning(); pl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
ps = Session(Tutor(pl, fake2, context=False), limit=3)
q1 = ps.next(); ps.give_up()
q2 = ps.next(); ps.answer('a score', confidence=60)       # a wrong try: the question stays open
t2 = Tutor(pl, fake2, context=False)                      # a restart: a new tutor with nothing open
back = Session.load(t2, ps.id)
test_eq((back.q.id, back.q.question, len(back.log), back.limit), (q2.id, q2.question, 1, 3))
assert 'answer' not in back.q and back.q.id in t2.open    # the learner view, and the full question in the tutor
test_eq(back.answer('the rank position', confidence=80).correct, True)
test_eq([(r['outcome'], r['floor0']) for r in back.log], [('gap', 0), ('fragile', 0)])
test_eq([t['who'] for t in back.log[-1]['turns']], ['tutor', 'you', 'tutor', 'you', 'tutor'])
```

[`moved`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#moved) gives
the floor before and after for each concept of the log.

``` python
test_eq([(m['concept'], m['before'], m['after'], m['asked'], m['passed']) for m in moved(back.log)], [('ranking', 0, 0, 2, 1)])
test_eq(moved([dict(concept='a', name='A', floor0=2, floor=3, correct=True), dict(concept='a', floor0=3, floor=4, correct=True, misconception='x')]),
        [dict(concept='a', name='A', before=2, after=4, asked=2, passed=2, misconceptions=['x'])])
```

`end` closes the session. An ended session loads with no open question
and gives no more questions.

``` python
back.next(); back.end()
again = Session.load(Tutor(pl, fake2, context=False), ps.id)
test_eq((again.q, again.next(), bool(again.ended)), (None, None, True))
test_is(Session.load(t2, 'nope'), None)
```

A session in a walk asks about the current step. When the step is
learned, it goes to the next step. It stops at the end of the walk.

``` python
jl = temp_learning()
for n in ('Tokenizers', 'Embeddings', 'Sandhi'): jl.put(n, f'{n} statement.', 'ml' if n != 'Sandhi' else 'sanskrit')
jl.update('sandhi', seen=1, due=1.)                     # a review due elsewhere does not break in
j = jl.put_journey(dict(id='llms', title='LLMs', goal='LLMs', steps=[dict(slug='tokenizers', status='todo'), dict(slug='embeddings', status='todo')]))
js = Session(Tutor(jl, fake2, context=False), journey='llms')
q = js.next()
test_eq((q.concept, q.why.split(';')[0]), ('tokenizers', 'the next step of your walk "LLMs"'))   # a method note can follow
js.give_up(); jl.update('tokenizers', floor=4)
test_eq(js.next().concept, 'embeddings')
js.give_up(); jl.update('embeddings', floor=4)
test_eq((js.next(), jl.session(js.id).journey), (None, 'llms'))
```

The profile goes into the question prompt. At the `gentle` pace a new
concept starts at depth 1, not 3.

``` python
gl2 = temp_learning(); gl2.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
gl2.set_profile(background='codes in Python', pace='gentle')
fk = Fake(dflt=dict(question='Which keeps its scale?', options=[dict(text='a rank', misconception=''), dict(text='a score', misconception='x')], correct=0, answer='', rubric=[]))
q = Tutor(gl2, fk, context=False).next()
test_eq(q.depth, 1)
assert 'codes in Python' in fk.calls[-1][0] and 'who' not in q
```

[`flow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#flow) moves
the pace by one step, and only from the last outcomes. A note comes only
when the pace changes.

``` python
sol, gap = dict(outcome='solid'), dict(outcome='gap')
test_eq(flow([]), ('steady', ''))
test_eq(flow([sol, gap, dict(outcome='misconception')]), ('gentle', 'easier: you missed the last two'))
test_eq(flow([sol] * 3, 'gentle'), ('steady', 'harder: 3 clean passes in a row'))
test_eq(flow([gap, gap], 'gentle'), ('gentle', ''))     # already gentle: no change, no note
test_eq(flow([sol, sol, gap]), ('steady', ''))           # one miss is not a trend
```

In a session, two misses make the next question easier, and its “why”
line says so.
[`Tutor.next`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor.next)
takes the pace from the session over the pace in the profile.

``` python
fw = temp_learning(); fw.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
fs = Session(Tutor(fw, fake2, context=False), limit=5)
for _ in range(2): fs.next(); fs.give_up()
test_eq(fs.next().why.endswith('; easier: you missed the last two'), True)
fw.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit')
test_eq(Tutor(fw, fake2, context=False).next(subject='sanskrit', pace='gentle').depth, 1)   # a new concept, at depth 1 and not 3
```

[`retests`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#retests)
keeps a miss until a pass comes at least `checks.retest` questions later
(2 by default). A new miss moves the concept to the end.

``` python
def lg(*xs): return [dict(concept=k, outcome=o, correct=o not in MISSES) for k, o in xs]
test_eq(retests(lg(('a', 'gap'), ('a', 'solid'))), {'a': 0})                          # a pass right after: still to retest
test_eq(retests(lg(('a', 'gap'), ('b', 'solid'), ('b', 'solid'), ('a', 'fragile'))), {})   # a later pass clears it
test_eq(retests(lg(('a', 'gap'), ('b', 'misconception'), ('a', 'gap'))), {'b': 1, 'a': 2})
```

When the questions left are only enough for the retests, the session
asks the missed concept again, and says why. With more questions left,
it does not.

``` python
rl = temp_learning(); rl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml', order=0); rl.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', order=1)
rs = Session(Tutor(rl, fake2, context=False), limit=4)
rs.log = lg(('ranking', 'gap'), ('sandhi', 'solid'), ('sandhi', 'solid'))
q = rs.next()
test_eq((q.concept, q.why), ('ranking', 'a retest: you missed this earlier in this session'))
rs.tutor.open.clear(); rs.limit = 10
assert not rs.next().why.startswith('a retest')
```

[`bridges`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#bridges)
takes known concepts only, from other subjects first. A transfer
question gets them in its prompt; an explain question does not.

``` python
bl = temp_learning()
bl.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml', related=['softmax'])
for n, s, f in (('Softmax', 'ml', 3), ('Ranking', 'ml', 4), ('Sandhi', 'sanskrit', 3), ('Nakshatra', 'jyotisha', 1)): bl.put(n, f'{n}.', s); bl.update(n.lower(), floor=f)
test_eq(bridges(bl.concept('attention'), bl.concepts()), ['Sandhi', 'Softmax', 'Ranking'])
fb = Fake(dflt=dict(question='Where else?', answer='', rubric=[]))
tb = Tutor(bl, fb, context=False)
tb.ask_on(bl.concept('attention'), 5); assert 'Sandhi' in fb.calls[-1][0]
tb.ask_on(bl.concept('attention'), 3); assert 'Sandhi' not in fb.calls[-1][0]
```

After each `observe_every` closed questions, the profile learns in the
background.

``` python
class Now:
    "A pool that runs a job at once, for the test."
    def submit(self, f, *a): f(*a)
ol = temp_learning(); ol.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
fo = Fake({**fake2.rules, 'You keep a short profile': dict(changes=[dict(field='confuses', add='ranks against scores', why='You missed it twice.')])}, dflt=fake2.dflt)
ot = Tutor(ol, fo, context=False, pool=Now(), observe_every=2)
for _ in range(2): ot.give_up(ot.next().id)
test_eq(ol.profile().confuses, ['ranks against scores'])
```

The sources of the learner ground the question, the grade and the
lesson. First, import
[`passage`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/ground.html#passage),
which makes one passage of a source.

``` python
from abhyasa.ground import passage
```

A source of notes grounds the question. The learner sees the citations
only when the question closes.

``` python
class Notes:
    name = 'notes'
    def search(self, q, k=4): return L([passage('vault:notes', 'n1', 'My ranking notes', 'Ranking orders items; RRF adds 1/(k + rank).')])
gl = temp_learning(); gl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
gt = Tutor(gl, fake2, sources=[Notes()])
q = gt.next()
assert 'My ranking notes' in fake2.calls[-1][0]                 # the question prompt has the passage
assert 'grounds' not in q and 'ctx' not in q                  # the learner does not see it yet
r = gt.answer(q.id, 'the rank position', confidence=80)
test_eq(r.grounds, [dict(src='vault:notes', ref='n1', title='My ranking notes', url='')])
assert 'My ranking notes' in fake2.calls[-1][0]                 # the grade prompt has it too
```

A function in `CLOSE_HOOKS` sees each closed question and can add to the
result. The result names its concept.

``` python
seen = []
def spy(t, q, r): seen.append(q.concept); r.extra = 1
CLOSE_HOOKS.append(spy)
try: r = gt.answer(gt.next().id, 'the rank position', confidence=80)
finally: CLOSE_HOOKS.remove(spy)
test_eq((seen, r.extra, r.concept), (['ranking'], 1, 'ranking'))
```

A function in `LESSON_HOOKS` picks the way of the lesson after a miss.
The lesson prompt uses that way, and the attempt keeps it in
`teach_method`. The miss still counts for the way of the question.

``` python
def by_analogy(t, q): return 'analogy'
LESSON_HOOKS.append(by_analogy)
try: q = gt.ask_on(gl.concept('ranking'), 2); r = gt.give_up(q.id)
finally: LESSON_HOOKS.remove(by_analogy)
a = gl.attempts(limit=1)[0]
assert way('analogy') in fake2.calls[-1][0]
test_eq((r.lesson_way, a.teach_method, a.method), ('analogy', 'analogy', q.method))
```

With no hook, the lesson uses the way of the question, and
[`lesson_way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/demo.html#lesson_way)
is empty.

``` python
q = gt.ask_on(gl.concept('ranking'), 2); r = gt.give_up(q.id)
test_eq((r.lesson_way, 'teach_method' in gl.attempts(limit=1)[0]), ('', False))
```

A follow-up is only what the learner says this time. The grade prompt
has the earlier turns in order, then the follow-up. A pass on the third
message, after two nudges, is `fragile`.

``` python
tl = temp_learning(); tl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
tt = Tutor(tl, fake, context=False)
q = tt.next()
tt.answer(q.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=60)
tt.answer(q.id, 'scale them first', confidence=60)
r = tt.answer(q.id, 'use the rank position', confidence=70)
p = next(c[0] for c in reversed(fake.calls) if 'You grade' in c[1])
assert p.index('Tutor (question)') < p.index('Learner: sum the scores') < p.index('Tutor (nudge)') < p.index('Learner: scale them first')
test_eq(p.split("Learner's answer: ")[1].split('\n')[0], 'use the rank position')   # only the follow-up
assert 'scale them first' not in p.split("Learner's answer")[1]
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.outcome), (True, True, 'fragile'))
```

## Teach on request

After a shaky pass, a lesson comes only when you ask. It leaves the
learner state as the close left it, and a second ask gives the same
lesson.

``` python
sl = temp_learning(); sl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
ss = Session(Tutor(sl, fake, context=False), limit=3)
q = ss.next()
for a in ('sum the scores', 'scale them first', 'use the rank position'): r = ss.answer(a, confidence=70)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'fragile'))
before = dict(sl.concept('ranking'))
```

The lesson builds on the first error, and the concept does not change.

``` python
lesson = ss.teach(q.id)
assert 'Check:' in lesson and 'could not' not in lesson
test_eq({k: v for k, v in sl.concept('ranking').items()}, before)
test_eq(ss.teach(q.id), lesson)
test_eq(len([x for x in ss.tutor.shut[q.id].turns if x.get('kind') == 'lesson']), 1)
```

The session log keeps the lesson, so a restart shows it.

``` python
test_eq(sl.session(ss.id).log[-1]['turns'][-1], dict(who='tutor', kind='lesson', text=lesson, method=ss.tutor.shut[q.id].method))
```

The grading prompt tells the model to explain a term that you say you do
not know, and to read past speech-to-text noise.

``` python
assert "I don't know what the loop means" in GRADE_SP and 'speech to text' in GRADE_SP
```

A right equation meets a rubric point, even when the words of the method
are missing. A right answer gets a grade of 7 or more. The grading
prompt says so. It also asks for the voice of a kind teacher, not a
report: “The key does not have to be a short form of the value”, not
“You assume that the key must be a condensed version of the value”.

``` python
for s in ('contains or implies it', 'need not say each step in words', 'only the method or framing', '7-10', 'When `correct` is false, `grade` is 6 or less.', 'A right result from wrong reasoning is not correct.'):
    assert s in GRADE_SP, s
assert 'not like a report' in GRADE_SP and 'BAD: "You assume' in GRADE_SP and 'kind, clear person' in TUTOR_SP   # the voice of a person, not a report
```

The question prompt asks for rubric points that are ideas. A point is
never a required word or a step of a named method.

``` python
assert 'Never make a rubric point a required word' in question_prompt(lr.concept('ranking'), 3)
```

## Short questions and short nudges

A question asks one thing, and a nudge after a wrong try is short.
`QUESTION_RULES` gives the rules for a question, with pairs of a bad and
a good question. The pairs use other subjects, so that they do not leak
into a real question.

``` python
p = question_prompt(lr.concept('ranking'), 2, method='code')
assert QUESTION_RULES in p
for s in ('one question mark', '"Then" or "Also"', 'under 60 words', 'one question word', '"and why"', 'ASD-STE100', '`question`, `options` and `answer`'): assert s in p, s
```

Each rule has one pair: a BAD question and a GOOD question. There are at
least four pairs, and no pair is about the neuron.

``` python
test_eq(QUESTION_RULES.count('BAD:'), QUESTION_RULES.count('GOOD:'))
assert QUESTION_RULES.count('GOOD:') >= 4 and 'neuron' not in QUESTION_RULES.lower()
```

A nudge says in a few words what is right, then asks one question. It
shows at most 4 lines of code, and never code that the thread already
shows.

``` python
for s in ('ONE question', 'at most 4 lines', 'Never repeat code', 'does not force code'): assert s in GRADE_SP, s
```

The way to teach still goes into the grade prompt. With the code way,
the prompt asks for code in `feedback` only when it helps the next step.

``` python
gq = AttrDict(name='Ranking', depth=2, question='Why ranks?', answer='', rubric=['ranks'], turns=[], method='code')
gp = grade_prompt(gq, 'because')
assert METHODS['code'] in gp and 'only when it helps the next step' in gp
assert 'Write `feedback` in this way.' not in gp
```

[`with_code`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#with_code)
still puts the code of a question first, in its own fenced block.

``` python
test_eq(with_code('What does s hold before the return line?', 's = 0\nreturn s'), '```python\ns = 0\nreturn s\n```\n\nWhat does s hold before the return line?')
```

## Best try counts

A try with a grade of `checks.near` or more shows that the learner has
the idea. If the question later closes as a miss, it closes as `fragile`
instead. The lesson still shows when the tutor teaches. The concept
keeps its floor and its ceiling. A model that grades each try with a set
grade plays the tutor here.

``` python
test_eq(val('checks.near'), 7)
def model(*gs):
    "A fake model whose grader gives the grades `gs` in turn, all as not correct."
    it = iter(gs)
    bad = lambda p, sp: dict(correct=False, grade=next(it), first_error='You do not name the method.', misconception='', feedback='Say it in words.')
    return Fake({**fake.rules, 'You grade one answer': bad})
def miss_after(*gs, give_up=True):
    "Try once for each grade in `gs`, then ask for the lesson. The result and the concept, with a floor of 2 before."
    l = temp_learning(); l.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml'); l.update('ranking', floor=2)
    bt = Tutor(l, model(*gs), context=False); q = bt.next()
    for g in gs[:2 if give_up else 3]: r = bt.answer(q.id, 'a try', confidence=40)
    return (bt.give_up(q.id) if give_up else r), l.concept('ranking'), q
```

Each try keeps its grade. A try graded 8 is the best try, so the lesson
still shows, but the outcome is `fragile` and the floor and the ceiling
stay.

``` python
r, c, q = miss_after(8)
test_eq([x['grade'] for x in q.tries], [8])
test_eq((r.done, r.correct, r.outcome), (True, True, 'fragile'))
assert 'Check:' in r.lesson
test_eq((r.feedback, r.first_error, r.misconception), ('', '', ''))   # no wrong-reply nudge under the pass
test_eq((c.floor, c.ceiling, c.misses), (2, 6, 0))
```

A best try of 3 is no near pass. The question still closes as a gap, and
the ceiling falls.

``` python
r, c, q = miss_after(3)
test_eq((r.correct, r.outcome), (False, 'gap'))
test_eq((c.floor, c.ceiling, c.misses), (2, 4, 1))
```

The third wrong try counts the same way. A grade of 8 in an earlier try
saves it. Grades of 3, 3 and 3 do not.

``` python
r, c, q = miss_after(3, 8, 3, give_up=False)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'fragile'))
test_eq([x['grade'] for x in q.tries], [3, 8, 3])
test_eq((r.feedback, r.first_error), ('', ''))   # the third reply was wrong: its nudge does not show
r, c, q = miss_after(3, 3, 3, give_up=False)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'gap'))
```

A try with no grade is no near pass.

``` python
r, c, q = miss_after(None)
test_eq((r.correct, r.outcome), (False, 'gap'))
```

## Ways to learn, and gaps you name

Each question gets a method. The prompt says it, and the outcome counts
for it when the question closes.

``` python
import random
```

``` python
wl = temp_learning(); wl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
seen = []
def wgrade(p, sp):
    seen.append(p); said = p.split("Learner's answer:")[1].split("Learner's think-aloud:")[0]
    if 'the loop' in said: return dict(correct=False, grade=2, first_error='You skip the sum.', misconception='', feedback='A loop adds each product.',
                                    gaps=['weighted sum as a loop'], asks_for='code')
    return dict(correct='rank position' in said, grade=8, first_error='', misconception='', feedback='Yes.', gaps=[], asks_for='')
wfake = Fake({'You grade one answer': wgrade, 'The idea: weighted sum as a loop': dict(name='Weighted sum as a loop', statement='A loop adds each weight times its input.'),
              'Teach the smallest step': 'Positions are shared. Check: what if k = 0?',
              'Write ONE question': lambda p, sp: seen.append(p) or dict(question='Why do ranks merge well?', answer='They are comparable.', rubric=['comparable'])})
wt = Tutor(wl, wfake, context=False); wt.rng = random.Random(1)
q = wt.next()
assert q.method in METHODS and f"The way to teach this time: {METHODS[q.method]}" in seen[-1]
```

“I don’t know what the loop means” keeps the idea as a gap of the
concept, and “show me with code” switches the method for the next nudge.

``` python
r = wt.answer(q.id, "I don't know what the loop means, show me with code")
test_eq(wl.concept('ranking').gaps, ['weighted-sum-as-a-loop'])
test_eq(wt.open[q.id].method, 'code')
test_eq(wl.attempts('ranking')[0].gaps, ['weighted sum as a loop'])
r = wt.answer(q.id, 'use the rank position')
assert METHODS['code'] in seen[-1]
```

A way that a session cannot show, such as `demo`, does not change the
method. A way that it can show does.

``` python
hq = AttrDict(method='words', gaps=[])
wt._heard(hq, dict(asks_for='demo')); test_eq(hq.method, 'words')
wt._heard(hq, dict(asks_for='code')); test_eq(hq.method, 'code')
```

The close counts the outcome for the method. The gap now comes first on
the concept.

``` python
test_eq(wl.stats().methods['ml']['code'], [.5, .5])   # a pass after a wrong try is shaky: half a credit
test_eq(wt.next(focus='ranking').concept, 'weighted-sum-as-a-loop')
```

“Another way” writes a new lesson in a method not used yet on that
question, and records the request on the attempt.

``` python
l1 = wt.teach(q.id); l2 = wt.teach(q.id, another=True)
ms = [x['method'] for x in wt.shut[q.id].turns if x.get('kind') == 'lesson']
test_eq((len(ms), ms[0] != ms[1]), (2, True))
test_eq(wl.attempts('ranking')[0].taught, 2)
test_eq(wl.stats().methods['ml']['code'], [.5, .5])   # a lesson on request changes no counts
```

A drill session takes the weak concept first, says why, and keeps the
drill after a restart.

``` python
dl = temp_learning(); dl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml'); dl.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit')
dl.update('sandhi', misses=2, misconceptions=['vowels never change'], seen=2)
ds = Session(Tutor(dl, fake, context=False), drill=True, limit=4)
q = ds.next()
test_eq((q.concept, q.why.split(';')[0]), ('sandhi', 'a weak spot: a misconception: vowels never change'))
test_eq(Session.load(ds.tutor, ds.id).drill, True)
```

## Prompts that you change in Settings

Each prompt starts with its default text from code. Thus the constants
and the prompts are the same until you save a text.

``` python
from abhyasa.prompts import PROMPTS, set_prompt, lines
from abhyasa.voice import settings
```

``` python
test_eq([prompt(n) for n in ('tutor', 'question', 'grade', 'lesson')], [TUTOR_SP, QUESTION_RULES, GRADE_SP, TEACH])
test_eq((lines(prompt('hints')), hints(), way('code')), (list(HINTS), HINTS, METHODS['code']))
assert {'tutor', 'question', 'grade', 'hints', 'lesson', *(f'way.{m}' for m in METHODS)} <= set(PROMPTS)
```

A saved text is in the next prompt, with no restart. Here the question
rules and the tutor rules change, and the fake model gets the new text.

``` python
pl = temp_learning(); pl.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
pf = Fake(dflt=dict(question='Why do ranks merge well?', answer='', rubric=[]))
pt = Tutor(pl, pf, context=False)
set_prompt('question', 'Ask about one dog.'); set_prompt('tutor', 'Be brief.')
q = pt.next()
assert 'Ask about one dog.' in pf.calls[-1][0] and QUESTION_RULES not in pf.calls[-1][0]
test_eq(pf.calls[-1][1], 'Be brief.')
```

A new hint ladder works on the next hint. A ladder that does not have 6
lines is refused, and the saved ladder stays.

``` python
set_prompt('hints', '\n'.join(f'Rung {i}.' for i in range(1, 7)))
pt.hint(q.id); assert 'Rung 1.' in pf.calls[-1][0]
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('hints', 'Only one line.'), contains='needs 6 lines')
test_eq(hints()[0], 'Rung 1.')
```

The text of a way goes into the next prompt too. A lesson instruction
without the ‘Check:’ line is refused, because the next question comes
from that line.

``` python
set_prompt('way.code', 'Use one short line of code.')
assert 'The way to teach this time: Use one short line of code.' in question_prompt(pl.concept('ranking'), 2, method='code')
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('lesson', 'Teach it.'), contains='Check:')
```

An empty text clears a saved text, so each prompt uses its default
again.

``` python
for n in ('question', 'tutor', 'hints', 'way.code'): set_prompt(n, '')
test_eq((prompt('question'), prompt('tutor'), hints(), way('code'), settings()['prompts']), (QUESTION_RULES, TUTOR_SP, HINTS, METHODS['code'], {}))
```

## Open questions after a restart

The tutor keeps each open question on the shelf as a document of kind
`open-q`. A restart of the app makes a new
[`Tutor`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/tutor.html#tutor) with
nothing in memory. The tutor then loads the question from the shelf,
with its tries and hints, and the learner can go on.

The tests change one setting, so import the setting tools.

``` python
from abhyasa.settings import SETTINGS, set_val, reset
```

Open a question with a walk step in its meta. Give one wrong try and get
one hint. The shelf keeps the question, the step, the try, the hint and
the confidence.

``` python
ol = temp_learning(); ol.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
ot = Tutor(ol, fake, context=False)
oq = ot.ask_on(ol.concept('ranking'), 3, meta=dict(walk='w1', step=0))
ot.answer(oq.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=40); ot.hint(oq.id)
m = ol.open_q(oq.id)
test_eq((m.status, m.walk, m.step, m.concept, m.confidence), ('open', 'w1', 0, 'ranking', 40))
test_eq((len(m.q['tries']), len(m.q['hints']), m.q['question']), (1, 1, oq.question))
assert {'answer', 'rubric'} <= set(m.q)   # the answer key stays on the server
```

A new tutor on the same shelf starts with nothing in memory. It finds
the question when you ask for it.

``` python
ot2 = Tutor(ol, fake, context=False)
test_eq(len(ot2.open), 0)
assert oq.id in ot2.open and ot2.open[oq.id].hints == ['Look at what the two lists have in common.']
```

The next wrong try counts as the second try, and the grader sees the
first try in the thread.

``` python
r = ot2.answer(oq.id, 'add the raw numbers', confidence=50)
test_eq((r.done, r.tries_left), (False, 1))
assert 'sum the scores' in fake.calls[-1][0]
test_eq(len(ol.open_q(oq.id).q['tries']), 2)
```

A pass closes the question. The shelf keeps it as closed, and a third
tutor does not open it again.

``` python
r = ot2.answer(oq.id, 'use the rank position', confidence=80)
test_eq((r.done, r.outcome), (True, 'fragile'))
test_eq((ol.open_q(oq.id).status, ol.open_q(oq.id).end), ('closed', 'closed'))
ot3 = Tutor(ol, fake, context=False)
assert oq.id not in ot3.open and ot3.open.get(oq.id) is None
test_fail(lambda: ot3.answer(oq.id, 'late'), contains=oq.id)
```

Search does not find an open question. Its meta has the answer key.

``` python
assert not [h for h in ol.search('Why does RRF use ranks, not scores?', limit=20) if h['kind'] == 'open-q']
```

## Old open questions

An open question with no change in `checks.open_days` days (7 by
default) closes as abandoned when a tutor loads it. It gets no grade and
it does not change the concept.

``` python
test_eq((val('checks.open_days'), SETTINGS['checks.open_days'].lo, SETTINGS['checks.open_days'].hi), (7, 1, 60))
xq = ot.ask_on(ol.concept('ranking'), 3); ot.answer(xq.id, 'sum the scores', confidence=40)
before, n = dict(ol.concept('ranking')), len(ol.attempts('ranking', limit=None))
ol.v.set_meta(ol.open_q(xq.id).doc_id, updated=time.time() - 8 * 86400)
assert xq.id not in Tutor(ol, fake, context=False).open
test_eq((ol.open_q(xq.id).status, ol.open_q(xq.id).end), ('closed', 'abandoned'))
test_eq((dict(ol.concept('ranking')), len(ol.attempts('ranking', limit=None))), (before, n))
```

With a longer setting, the same age is not too old.

``` python
yq = ot.ask_on(ol.concept('ranking'), 3)
ol.v.set_meta(ol.open_q(yq.id).doc_id, updated=time.time() - 8 * 86400)
set_val('checks.open_days', 10)
try: assert yq.id in Tutor(ol, fake, context=False).open
finally: reset('checks.open_days')
```

## A session after a restart

A session question keeps its hints after a restart. `end` closes the
question on the shelf.

``` python
sl2 = temp_learning(); sl2.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
s1 = Session(Tutor(sl2, fake2, context=False), limit=3)
sq = s1.next(); s1.hint()
back2 = Session.load(Tutor(sl2, fake2, context=False), s1.id)
test_eq((back2.q.id, len(back2.tutor.open[sq.id].hints)), (sq.id, 1))
back2.end()
test_eq((sl2.open_q(sq.id).status, sl2.open_q(sq.id).end), ('closed', 'dropped'))
test_eq(Session.load(Tutor(sl2, fake2, context=False), s1.id).q, None)
```

An old vault has no `open-q` documents, and its session document has the
full open question. That question still loads, and the shelf then keeps
it.

``` python
sl3 = temp_learning(); sl3.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
s3 = Session(Tutor(sl3, fake2, context=False), limit=3); q3 = s3.next()
sl3.v.set_meta(sl3.session(s3.id).doc_id, open=dict(s3.tutor.open[q3.id]))   # an old vault: the full question in the session document
sl3.v.forget(sl3.open_q(q3.id).doc_id)
back3 = Session.load(Tutor(sl3, fake2, context=False), s3.id)
test_eq((back3.q.id, sl3.open_q(q3.id).status), (q3.id, 'open'))
```

A session document with a closed question does not open it again.

``` python
sl3.put_open_q(back3.tutor.open[q3.id], 'closed', 'closed')
test_eq(Session.load(Tutor(sl3, fake2, context=False), s3.id).q, None)
```

## One caller at a time

Two tabs can send an answer to the same question at the same time. The
lock of the question lets one caller work on it at a time. To make the
overlap sure, this grader waits a moment before it grades.

These tests use threads and the garbage collector.

``` python
import gc, threading as th
```

``` python
def slow(p, sp):
    time.sleep(.2)
    ok = 'rank position' in p.split("Learner's answer:")[1]
    return dict(correct=ok, grade=8 if ok else 3, first_error='You add raw scores.', misconception='', feedback='Look again.')
slow_fake = Fake({'You grade one answer': slow}, dflt=dict(question='Why ranks?', answer='Positions.', rubric=['positions']))
def both(f, *args):
    "Run `f(*a)` for each `a` in `args` in two threads at once. Return the results; a KeyError is the result `'gone'`."
    out = [None] * len(args)
    def go(k):
        try: out[k] = f(*args[k])
        except KeyError: out[k] = 'gone'
    ts = [th.Thread(target=go, args=(k,)) for k in range(len(args))]
    for x in ts: x.start()
    for x in ts: x.join()
    return out
```

After a restart, two wrong tries at once both count. The tutor loads one
copy of the question, so no try is lost.

``` python
cl_ = temp_learning(); cl_.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
cq = Tutor(cl_, slow_fake, context=False).ask_on(cl_.concept('ranking'), 3)
ct = Tutor(cl_, slow_fake, context=False)   # a restart
set_val('checks.tries', 5)
try: rs = both(lambda a: ct.answer(cq.id, a), ('a sum',), ('a mean',))
finally: reset('checks.tries')
test_eq(sorted(r.tries_left for r in rs), [3, 4])
test_eq(sorted(t['answer'] for t in cl_.open_q(cq.id).q['tries']), ['a mean', 'a sum'])
```

Two right answers at once close the question one time. The second caller
finds no open question and gets a `KeyError`, which a page shows as a
closed check.

``` python
rs = both(lambda a: ct.answer(cq.id, a), ('the rank position',), ('the rank position',))
test_eq(sorted(map(str, [r if r == 'gone' else r.done for r in rs])), ['True', 'gone'])
test_eq(len([a for a in cl_.attempts('ranking', limit=None) if a.get('final')]), 1)
```

The session document keeps only the learner view of its open question,
with no answer key. The open-q document has the full question.

``` python
s4 = Session(Tutor(cl_, fake2, context=False), limit=3); q4 = s4.next()
o = cl_.session(s4.id).open
assert o['id'] == q4.id and 'answer' not in o and 'rubric' not in o and 'answer' in cl_.open_q(q4.id).q
```

A learner view in a session document never opens as a question. With no
open-q document, the session loads with no open question.

``` python
cl_.v.forget(cl_.open_q(q4.id).doc_id)
test_eq(Session.load(Tutor(cl_, fake2, context=False), s4.id).q, None)
```

The locks do not grow without end: a lock that no caller holds goes
away.

``` python
gc.collect()
assert cq.id not in _QLOCKS and len(_QLOCKS) < 5
```
